column1: # iota(4,11) >= 32 ?  the deg(0) = 13 cube, one line per degree-sequence sub-cube.
# Written by `iota_sym --checkpoint`; a line is appended the moment a
# sub-cube lands, so a reclaimed container loses only what was in flight.
# THE CUBE IS UNSAT ONLY WHEN ALL 1939 SUB-CUBES ARE UNSAT. Resume with
# the same --checkpoint: rows marked UNSAT or SAT are skipped, rows marked
# UNKNOWN are re-run, because UNKNOWN is a budget and not a verdict.
# The split is the two-block degree sequence of symbreak::sequence_cubes:
# positions 0..b-1 are non-increasing from deg(0), the ceiling resets to
# deg(0) at position b, and positions b..g-1 are non-increasing again.
# An independent enumeration of that model reproduces 1939 here and the
# 19 that iota4_11.tsv records at deg(0) = 12, which is the cross-check
# that the split is a cover.  Corrected counts, superseding the figures
# an earlier session quoted from a globally-sorted model:
# Measured cost of a sub-cube, same two sub-cubes, both solvers:
#   [.. 10, 1]  cadical UNSAT 128.6s   cryptominisat5 UNSAT 269.6s
#   [.. 9,  2]  cadical UNKNOWN @300s  cryptominisat5 UNSAT 420.6s
# Neither solver dominates. At ~300 s a sub-cube, 1939 of them is about
# 40 core-hours, i.e. ~10 h wall on four cores if every one lands.
# sub-cube
